analysis.title: Shell Plc: A portfolio built to pay
key_insights: Barclays keeps Shell at Overweight with an unchanged GBP 49.50 price target (+25.1% upside from GBP 39.57 on 28-Oct-26) and an unchanged Positive industry view on European Integrated Energy.

Shell raised its 4Q26 buyback to $5bn from $3bn in 3Q26 to keep distributions within its 40-50% CFFO payout framework, which management called sacrosanct through the cycle. Management framed it as not necessarily a new quarterly run-rate.

Barclays now models 20% y/y DPS growth in 2027 as its base case. Buybacks have been about 60% of shareholder distributions over the past four years, and Shell's 2026E dividend yield of 3.0% is the lowest in the European energy peer group (average 4.9%).

Growth supports the outlook into the next decade: ARC Resources (acquired 2 September 2026) adds a long-life, low-cost resource base. The September FID on LNG Canada Phase 2 adds nearly 6mtpa of LNG from the early 2030s. Management expects ARC to fit within the existing capex framework.
Upstream catalysts ahead: Bay du Nord is targeting FID early in 2027 and Bonga Southwest could follow next year, subject to conditions aligning. Namibia exploration wells are upcoming.

Middle East recovery is gradual: one Pearl GTL train has partly restarted, which initially supports inventory rebuilding. The second train is targeted to be ready for start-up late in 1Q27, and further recovery depends on export access.
Integration between assets and trading is improving refinery optimisation. Higher freight costs could weigh on realised margins in 4Q26.

3Q26 adjusted earnings were $10,814m, 5% above both Barclays ($10,346m) and consensus ($10,329m). Adjusted EPS was $1.93 vs Barclays $1.79. Upstream EBITDA beat consensus by 9% and Chemicals and Products by 7%, while Marketing missed consensus by 5%.
3Q26 reported CFO was $21,043m vs consensus $16,546m (+27%). Cash capex rose to $7,922m from $4,031m in 2Q26. Net debt incl. leases fell to $39,733m and gearing to 16.6%.

Barclays cut 2026E EPS to $6.69 from $6.79 and 2027E EPS to $7.51 from $7.71, on model changes and a lower refining margin assumption (2026E $27.4/bl vs $30.0/bl before). Barclays 2026E-2028E EPS is above Bloomberg consensus ($6.23, $5.42, $4.87).

Valuation is by sum-of-the-parts: upstream DCF at a 10% discount rate with Brent at $95/bl for 2027, $80/bl to 2030 and $70/bl long run. Refining is valued at 5x EBITDA, chemicals 4x, retail and lubricants 12x, renewables 10x. Upside case assumes oil above $100/bl long term (GBP 61.00), downside case $50/bl (GBP 23.00).

market_movers.rationale: Overweight maintained on near-term high free cash flow yield, potential for larger buybacks and a rising dividend. The price target is unchanged at GBP 49.50 (+25.1%).

sector_views.rationale: Barclays Industry View is Positive (unchanged), with Shell rated Overweight within the coverage universe.

earnings_insights: Shell 3Q26 reported adjusted earnings $10,814m vs Barclays est $10,346m and consensus est $10,329m (+5% vs both). Adjusted EPS reported $1.93 vs Barclays est $1.79.
Shell 3Q26 reported CFO $21,043m vs consensus est $16,546m (+27%). CFFO ex working capital before interest $21,239m vs consensus est $18,178m (+17%).

Shell 3Q26 Upstream adjusted EBITDA reported $9,269m vs consensus est $8,506m (+9%). Chemicals and Products reported $6,201m vs consensus est $5,805m (+7%). Marketing reported $1,986m vs consensus est $2,094m (-5%).
Shell 3Q26 dividend reported at $0.391 per share (3Q25: $0.358). 3Q26 production was 2,574 kboe/d, down 7% y/y.

Barclays estimates 2026E adjusted EPS $6.69 (previously $6.79), 2027E $7.51 (previously $7.71) and 2028E $4.98 (previously $5.11). Bloomberg consensus est is $6.23, $5.42 and $4.87. Barclays 2026E dividend is $3.2/share, 2027E raised to $3.8 from $3.5.

4Q26 guidance: Integrated Gas production 1,080-1,180 kboe/d, upstream production 1,700-1,900 kboe/d, LNG liquefaction 7.3-7.9Mt, refinery utilisation 92%-100%, FY26 cash capex $23-25bn, corporate adjusted earnings a net expense of $600-800m.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Realised Brent fell 6% q/q but is up 34% y/y, supporting the strong 3Q26 earnings and cash flow.
Barclays models Brent falling after 2027, which drives EPS to fall from $7.51 in 2027E to $4.98 in 2028E.
Barclays lowered its refining margin assumption for 2026, trimming its 2026 EPS.

risk_factors: Higher freight costs could weigh on realised margins in 4Q26.
Further Middle East recovery depends on export access, and the second Pearl GTL train is not targeted to start up until late 1Q27.
Barclays' price target and rating depend on its estimates of profitability, cash flow, oil prices and downstream margins. A downside case with oil at $50/bl long term gives GBP 23.00.
Shell has significant production exposure to Nigeria relative to other companies.
Upstream and downstream operations are subject to planned and unplanned downtime, and OPEC actions can affect the oil market.

Figure 2 ranks 2026E dividend yield across European energy names, with Shell lowest at 3.0% and Var Energi highest at 9.5%.
geopolitical: Middle East recovery at Shell's Pearl GTL remains gradual and depends on export access.
The report notes the CEO referred to more structural stability in the oil price.
